**Comparability note:** All five filers are calendar-year (Jan 1–Dec 31) FY2024 registrants, so the fiscal periods align [DOC-1]. However, **Alaska's FY2024 is not a like-for-like standalone period**: Alaska completed its acquisition of Hawaiian Holdings on September 18, 2024, and Hawaiian's results are consolidated only from that date forward, contributing $869M of revenue and a $113M net loss to the FY2024 consolidated figures [DOC-2]. Alaska's FY2024 therefore blends ~8.5 months of standalone Alaska with ~3.5 months of the combined entity, so its margins are neither comparable to its own prior year nor a clean full-year read versus peers. Excluding Hawaiian, Alaska's implied net margin would be roughly 4.7% ($508M / $10,866M) rather than 3.4% — enough to change its position relative to Southwest/American but not enough to displace Delta or United.

**Operating margin, FY2024 (operating income ÷ total operating revenue)**

| Rank | Airline | Calculation | Margin |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Delta | $5,995M / $61,643M [DOC-1] | 9.7% |
| 2 | United | $5,096M / $57,063M [DOC-1] | 8.9% |
| 3 | Alaska | $570M / $11,735M [DOC-1] | 4.86% |
| 4 | American | $2,614M / $54,211M [DOC-1] | 4.82% |
| 5 | Southwest | $321M / $27,483M [DOC-1] | 1.2% |

The Alaska/American ordering is effectively a tie (4 basis points apart) and is sensitive to the Hawaiian consolidation effect [DOC-2].

**Net margin, FY2024 (net income ÷ total operating revenue)**

| Rank | Airline | Calculation | Margin |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Delta | $3,457M / $61,643M [DOC-1] | 5.6% |
| 2 | United | $3,149M / $57,063M [DOC-1] | 5.5% |
| 3 | Alaska | $395M / $11,735M [DOC-1] | 3.4% |
| 4 | Southwest | $465M / $27,483M [DOC-1] | 1.7% |
| 5 | American | $846M / $54,211M [DOC-1] | 1.6% |

**Is the top-ranked airline the same?** Yes — Delta ranks first on both operating margin (9.7%) and net margin (5.6%) [DOC-1], with United a close second on both. The rankings diverge only in the lower half: American places 4th on operating margin but last on net margin, because its below-the-line costs (principally interest expense on its debt load) consume the bulk of its operating profit, while Southwest's net income ($465M) actually exceeded its operating income ($321M) [DOC-1], lifting it above American on a net basis.

ANSWER: Operating margin: Delta 9.7% > United 8.9% > Alaska 4.86% > American 4.82% > Southwest 1.2%. Net margin: Delta 5.6% > United 5.5% > Alaska 3.4% > Southwest 1.7% > American 1.6%. Yes — Delta is top-ranked in both (note: Alaska's FY2024 includes Hawaiian only from Sept 18, 2024, so its margins are not fully comparable).
